k: The Hierophant asked us to wait with the ship. He said tonight we would see the most beautiful sunset of our lives.
src: 'The Hierophant asked us to wait with the ship. He said tonight we would see the most beautiful sunset of our lives.'

k: He said, "Remember it."
src: 'He said, "Remember it."'

k: ...Why would he tell us to remember it?
src: '...Why would he tell us to remember it?'

k: Tobias won't come in for supper. Says the boat needs readying. He's readied it four times.
src: 'Tobias won\'t come in for supper. Says the boat needs readying. He\'s readied it four times.'

k: Talk to him, Wren. He listens to Halloways. Always did.
src: 'Talk to him, Wren. He listens to Halloways. Always did.'

k: The village well. WREN + ILSE + THE SEA, carved years ago. Underneath, freshly scratched, the knife marks still pale: + PIP.
src: 'The village well. WREN + ILSE + THE SEA, carved years ago. Underneath, freshly scratched, the knife marks still pale: + PIP.'

k: Wrong way, sparrow! The DOCKS!
src: 'Wrong way, sparrow! The DOCKS!'

k: The tide caves... Tobias would know if there's another way up. Ask him first.
src: 'The tide caves... Tobias would know if there\'s another way up. Ask him first.'

k: The tide caves. Not now. Mom first.
src: 'The tide caves. Not now. Mom first.'

k: No time! Down the hill!
src: 'No time! Down the hill!'

k: Letter
src: 'Letter'

k: Your own shelf. Every book on it washed up on the beach. You used to think the sea liked you.
src: 'Your own shelf. Every book on it washed up on the beach. You used to think the sea liked you.'

k: Your bed. Made. Mom made your bed. She never makes your bed.
src: 'Your bed. Made. Mom made your bed. She never makes your bed.'

k: Bread box
src: 'Bread box'

k: Ilse's herb jars, labeled in her tiny, exact handwriting. Nana has kept every one of them dusted while she was away.
src: 'Ilse\'s herb jars, labeled in her tiny, exact handwriting. Nana has kept every one of them dusted while she was away.'

k: The kettle. Nana Brisa has had it on the boil since yesterday noon, just in case.
src: 'The kettle. Nana Brisa has had it on the boil since yesterday noon, just in case.'

k: Wren, love! A bed and a bowl of chowder? Thirty gold. Prices went up — the sun's making everyone nervous.
src: 'Wren, love! A bed and a bowl of chowder? Thirty gold. Prices went up — the sun\'s making everyone nervous.'

k: the Gull's Rest
src: 'the Gull\'s Rest'

k: Forty years at sea, and I was never once frightened of calm water.
src: 'Forty years at sea, and I was never once frightened of calm water.'

k: Till today.
src: 'Till today.'

k: Wren! Homecoming special: everything's the same price as always.
src: 'Wren! Homecoming special: everything\'s the same price as always.'

k: A crate of salted fish and a note: "MAELA — DON'T." Below it: "I DID." Below that, newer: "TOBY — THE BOAT'S FINE. COME IN FOR SUPPER."
src: 'A crate of salted fish and a note: "MAELA — DON\'T." Below it: "I DID." Below that, newer: "TOBY — THE BOAT\'S FINE. COME IN FOR SUPPER."'

k: A charcoal sketch pinned over the stove: three skinny boys in a rowboat, grinning. Under each, a name: EDRIN. TOBY. FEN.
src: 'A charcoal sketch pinned over the stove: three skinny boys in a rowboat, grinning. Under each, a name: EDRIN. TOBY. FEN.'

k: The cot you have slept in for a year. Someone has patched the blanket a dozen times, with whatever was to hand. One patch is a piece of a Dawnguard flag.
src: 'The cot you have slept in for a year. Someone has patched the blanket a dozen times, with whatever was to hand. One patch is a piece of a Dawnguard flag.'

k: A pot of soup, gently burning. It smells of ash-potato and, very faintly, of fish.
src: 'A pot of soup, gently burning. It smells of ash-potato and, very faintly, of fish.'

k: Rock
src: 'Rock'

k: A cairn of stacked gray stones. Scratched on the flat stone at its foot: EDRIN HALLOWAY. HE'D WANT A BETTER STONE.
src: 'A cairn of stacked gray stones. Scratched on the flat stone at its foot: EDRIN HALLOWAY. HE\'D WANT A BETTER STONE.'

k: A newer cairn. The stones are still sharp-edged. YSOLDE HALLOWAY. KEEPER. SHE HELD.
src: 'A newer cairn. The stones are still sharp-edged. YSOLDE HALLOWAY. KEEPER. SHE HELD.'

k: A little fishing boat, upright on the ash, a long way from any water. Painted on the bow: THE SEAGULL. Fennick's boat. It rose with the sea, and came down here, with him.
src: 'A little fishing boat, upright on the ash, a long way from any water. Painted on the bow: THE SEAGULL. Fennick\'s boat. It rose with the sea, and came down here, with him.'

k: Fennick's garden. Ash-potatoes, a stubborn rosemary, and — tucked in a sheltered corner — one sprig of sea lavender, in a pot, carefully watered.
src: 'Fennick\'s garden. Ash-potatoes, a stubborn rosemary, and — tucked in a sheltered corner — one sprig of sea lavender, in a pot, carefully watered.'

k: A practice post, hacked half through. Fennick's been keeping his arm in. Or keeping busy.
src: 'A practice post, hacked half through. Fennick\'s been keeping his arm in. Or keeping busy.'

k: Not yet. Fennick wanted to show me something first.
src: 'Not yet. Fennick wanted to show me something first.'

k: LANTERNFALL — Westmost Light of Solmere.nThe chalk underneath has almost weathered away: ...ONIZATION IN PROGRE... KEEP TO YOUR HOMES.
src: 'LANTERNFALL — Westmost Light of Solmere.\nThe chalk underneath has almost weathered away: ...ONIZATION IN PROGRE... KEEP TO YOUR HOMES.'

k: The village well, torn up roots and all. WREN + ILSE + THE SEA + PIP. Somebody has added, in the last year, very small: COME HOME.
src: 'The village well, torn up roots and all. WREN + ILSE + THE SEA + PIP. Somebody has added, in the last year, very small: COME HOME.'

k: Table
src: 'Table'

k: Your bed, still made. Your mother made it the morning she wrote the letter. Nobody has slept in it since.
src: 'Your bed, still made. Your mother made it the morning she wrote the letter. Nobody has slept in it since.'

k: The cutter's mast, snapped clean. A Dawnguard pennant still flutters from the stump, red and gold, very bright against the ash.
src: 'The cutter\'s mast, snapped clean. A Dawnguard pennant still flutters from the stump, red and gold, very bright against the ash.'

k: A sheet of white Choir paper, the gold sunburst at its head:nTHE LAST STONE WAS GIVEN FREELY, BY THE KEEPER'S DAUGHTER OF LANTERNFALL.n— by order of His Radiance the Hierophant.nSomeone has drawn a noose underneath.
src:
'A sheet of white Choir paper, the gold sunburst at its head:
THE LAST STONE WAS GIVEN FREELY, BY THE KEEPER'S DAUGHTER OF LANTERNFALL.
— by order of His Radiance the Hierophant.
Someone has drawn a noose underneath.'

k: Don't steal, don't fight, don't fall off. That's the whole law.
src: 'Don\'t steal, don\'t fight, don\'t fall off. That\'s the whole law.'

k: Folk keep falling off. You'd think it'd be the easy one.
src: 'Folk keep falling off. You\'d think it\'d be the easy one.'

k: Warden says you're going east. Alone.
src: 'Warden says you\'re going east. Alone.'

k: I'll keep the soup warm. Hale says I'm not to say that. I said it anyway.
src: 'I\'ll keep the soup warm. Hale says I\'m not to say that. I said it anyway.'

k: East gate's shut. Strait's shut. Everything east of here's shut.
src: 'East gate\'s shut. Strait\'s shut. Everything east of here\'s shut.'

k: Warden Hale's orders. Ask at the big hull, north side.
src: 'Warden Hale\'s orders. Ask at the big hull, north side.'

k: Salvage and sundries! Everything I sell fell out of the sky, so it's all slightly dented.
src: 'Salvage and sundries! Everything I sell fell out of the sky, so it\'s all slightly dented.'

k: Some of it's even better than new. The sky's full of dead rich men's luggage.
src: 'Some of it\'s even better than new. The sky\'s full of dead rich men\'s luggage.'

k: Seven wounds in the sky, child. I count them every hour. Somebody has to.
src: 'Seven wounds in the sky, child. I count them every hour. Somebody has to.'

k: Six of them bleed white. One bleeds gold — far to the west, low down, near where Lanternfall was.
src: 'Six of them bleed white. One bleeds gold — far to the west, low down, near where Lanternfall was.'

k: Somebody over there is still holding on to something. Holding very, very hard.
src: 'Somebody over there is still holding on to something. Holding very, very hard.'

k: Twenty years a sailor out of Port Gale. Now look up. No — UP. See that shimmer, past the wounds?
src: 'Twenty years a sailor out of Port Gale. Now look up. No — UP. See that shimmer, past the wounds?'

k: That's the sea. All of it. Hanging up there, upside down, fish and all.
src: 'That\'s the sea. All of it. Hanging up there, upside down, fish and all.'

k: Now and then a fish falls out. Free dinner, if it doesn't land on you.
src: 'Now and then a fish falls out. Free dinner, if it doesn\'t land on you.'

k: Ash-potatoes. They grow in anything. Taste of nothing. Keep you alive.
src: 'Ash-potatoes. They grow in anything. Taste of nothing. Keep you alive.'

k: Like most things now, I suppose.
src: 'Like most things now, I suppose.'

k: We're playing Lost Wall! Kay writes letters and I deliver them. It's way better than the other game.
src: 'We\'re playing Lost Wall! Kay writes letters and I deliver them. It\'s way better than the other game.'

k: We're playing Catch the Keeper's Girl! You be her! You have to run, and if we catch you, we throw you off the edge!
src: 'We\'re playing Catch the Keeper\'s Girl! You be her! You have to run, and if we catch you, we throw you off the edge!'

k: ...PRETEND off the edge. Kay always cries if it's real off the edge.
src: '...PRETEND off the edge. Kay always cries if it\'s real off the edge.'

k: I don't like that game. I think the Keeper's girl was probably just sad.
src: 'I don\'t like that game. I think the Keeper\'s girl was probably just sad.'

k: Mama says sad people do stupid things. Mama did one once. She married Papa.
src: 'Mama says sad people do stupid things. Mama did one once. She married Papa.'

k: Trader, out of Kiteholm. North, past the wind-stacks. Town of kites and scrap.
src: 'Trader, out of Kiteholm. North, past the wind-stacks. Town of kites and scrap.'

k: A gang of orphans runs the scrap-yards there. Boss is a boy — twelve, maybe. Mouth like a sailor, fingers like a magpie. He took my purse, then gave it back because I "looked like I needed it more."
src: 'A gang of orphans runs the scrap-yards there. Boss is a boy — twelve, maybe. Mouth like a sailor, fingers like a magpie. He took my purse, then gave it back because I "looked like I needed it more."'

k: And a big blond sellsword who drinks too much and cries at sea shanties. Kiteholm's a strange place.
src: 'And a big blond sellsword who drinks too much and cries at sea shanties. Kiteholm\'s a strange place.'

k: I come out here to the edge every morning and I count to a hundred.
src: 'I come out here to the edge every morning and I count to a hundred.'

k: I don't jump. I just count. Then I go back and eat my soup.
src: 'I don\'t jump. I just count. Then I go back and eat my soup.'

k: It's a good number, a hundred. You should try it.
src: 'It\'s a good number, a hundred. You should try it.'

k: Letters, pinned three deep. "MAMA — I'M ON THE BIG ROCK. THERE'S SOUP." "TO WHOEVER HAS MY DOG: HIS NAME IS BISCUIT."
src: 'Letters, pinned three deep. "MAMA — I\'M ON THE BIG ROCK. THERE\'S SOUP." "TO WHOEVER HAS MY DOG: HIS NAME IS BISCUIT."'

k: "DAD — I KEPT THE BOAT. I KEPT IT. COME AND SEE." "To Corporal Hask, if you're alive: I forgive you for the thing with the goat."
src: '"DAD — I KEPT THE BOAT. I KEPT IT. COME AND SEE." "To Corporal Hask, if you\'re alive: I forgive you for the thing with the goat."'

k: Lost Wall
src: 'Lost Wall'
